rule: audit scope: "state that can desync", "races between concurrent requests for the same resource"; the sibling pump in router/mod.rs:266-274 and 500-514 shows the intended pattern (endpoint identity check plus self-removal on exit)
summary: `RemoteTerminalFrames` keys its frame pump by host only, never records which endpoint it is bound to, and never removes the entry when the pump task exits, so after a host's endpoint is replaced no new pump is ever started and remote terminals stop receiving frames permanently.
evidence:
crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/router/sessions.rs:21-23 — the pump entry carries no endpoint identity:
```rust
struct Pump {
    cancel: CancellationToken,
}
```
router/sessions.rs:62-63 — a pre-existing entry short-circuits pump creation unconditionally:
```rust
if pumps.contains_key(host) {
    return Ok(());
}
```
router/sessions.rs:105 — the task exits on a closed channel but leaves its map entry behind:
```rust
Err(tokio::sync::broadcast::error::RecvError::Closed) => break,
```
The only removal path is `detach` when the host's last attachment goes away (router/sessions.rs:113-118). Compare the endpoint event pump, which does both things right: `EndpointPump { endpoint, cancel }` with `Arc::ptr_eq(&current.endpoint, &endpoint)` before reusing (router/mod.rs:266-274) and `finish_pump(&event_pumps, &event_host, &event_endpoint)` after the loop breaks (router/mod.rs:320, 526-538).
Endpoints really are replaced: `Machines::rebuild` drops and closes an endpoint whose `HostConfigEntry` changed (crates/fleet-daemon/src/machines/registry.rs:74-89), and `reconcile_runtime_config` calls `rebuild` on every config change (crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/maintenance.rs:109).
failure_scenario: A user is attached to a terminal on host `dev-box` (a pump exists for `dev-box`, attachment count 1). The user edits the host's ssh address in settings. `reconcile_runtime_config` → `Machines::rebuild` drops the old endpoint and spawns `endpoint.close()`; the old endpoint's event broadcast sender is dropped, so the frames pump's `remote_events.recv()` returns `Closed` and the task `break`s — leaving `pumps["dev-box"]` in place with a cancelled-nobody token. The link comes back on the new endpoint, the client re-attaches, `forward` calls `sessions::on_attach` → `attach` increments the count, sees `pumps.contains_key("dev-box")`, and returns `Ok(())` without subscribing to the new endpoint. `Event::TerminalFrame` is explicitly skipped by the endpoint event pump (router/mod.rs:312-317), so nothing else relays it: the remote terminal renders the last frame it ever got and never updates again for the life of the daemon.
proposed_fix: Mirror `EndpointPump`: store `endpoint: Arc<dyn RemoteEndpoint>` in `Pump`, and in `attach` reuse the pump only when `Arc::ptr_eq(&current.endpoint, &endpoint)` — otherwise cancel it and spawn a new one. Add a `finish_pump`-style cleanup after the `loop` in the spawned task that removes the entry when it still points at this endpoint, so a `Closed` channel does not leave a tombstone.
test_plan: Extend `crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/router/sessions.rs`'s `mod tests` with `attach_rebinds_after_the_endpoint_is_replaced`: build a `FakeRemote` for host `devbox`, `on_attach`, assert a frame relays; then drop the first `FakeRemote` (closing its event sender), create a second `FakeRemote` for the same host, `on_attach` again with the new endpoint, `emit` a frame from it and expect it on the bus within a timeout. Before the fix the second `recv` times out; after the fix the frame arrives.
verify_reason: router/sessions.rs:21-23 (Pump holds only a cancel token), :62-63 (contains_key short-circuits with no endpoint check) and :113-118 (the sole removal path) match the finding exactly, and the sibling endpoint pump does both things right (router/mod.rs:266-274 Arc::ptr_eq reuse, :320 and :526-538 finish_pump). Endpoint replacement is real: machines/registry.rs:66-89 drops and closes an endpoint whose HostConfigEntry changed, and endpoint() then lazily builds a fresh RemoteLink (registry.rs:105-124). Down does NOT clear attachments — router/mod.rs:344-360 only records tombstones with attachment_count and clears ids — and Ready restores the same local ids (router/mod.rs:466-520), so the count stays >0 across the swap while the pump remains bound to the dead link. TerminalFrame is explicitly skipped by the endpoint pump (router/mod.rs:314-318), so nothing else relays frames. Correction to the evidence: the RecvError::Closed tombstone path (sessions.rs:105) is essentially unreachable — the spawned task moves the `endpoint` Arc in (used by request_full_frames at sessions.rs:98), so events_tx (machines/link.rs:101, 316-318) is never dropped and close() does not close it (link.rs:324-331). The stale pump therefore lives on forever rather than leaving a tombstone; same user-visible outcome, different mechanism.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/router/sessions.rs (Pump struct, attach, detach, the spawned task) and its inline mod tests at sessions.rs:~196. crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/router/mod.rs:150-157 passes the endpoint already, so no caller changes. crates/fleet-daemon/tests/router_core.rs and crates/fleet-daemon/src/testing/FakeRemote (install_endpoint at machines/registry.rs:127) are the places that exercise endpoint swaps.
corrected_fix: Store `endpoint: Arc<dyn RemoteEndpoint>` in Pump and, in attach, reuse only when Arc::ptr_eq matches, else cancel the old pump and spawn a new one for the new endpoint — mirroring router/mod.rs:266-274. The finish_pump-style cleanup after the loop is worth adding for the cancel path but must not be sold as the fix for RecvError::Closed, which cannot fire while the task holds the endpoint Arc. Note that cancelling the old pump must not touch `attached` (the counts must survive the rebind, or the restored terminal is filtered out by is_attached at sessions.rs:167-172).

rule: audit scope: "cleanup skipped on the error path", "state that can desync"
summary: `forward` only runs the detach bookkeeping when `attaching != response.is_ok()`, so a `DetachTerminal` that the remote rejects leaves the local attachment count above zero forever — the frames pump is never torn down and the terminal is falsely restored on reconnect.
failure_scenario: A remote terminal's shell exits and the remote daemon closes it (`close_terminal_if_present` removes it from `hosts`). The client, which still has it on screen, sends `DetachTerminal { terminal }`. The remote answers `NotFound`. Locally the count in `Attached::by_host["dev-box"][local]` stays at 1: (a) `is_attached` keeps returning true, so the pump keeps publishing any frame that still arrives for that id; (b) `detach` is never called with `empty == true`, so the host's frame pump is never cancelled even after every real client is gone; (c) on the next link Down, the tombstone builder filters on `attachment_count > 0` (router/mod.rs:344-354) and records a tombstone for the dead terminal, so `restore_attached_sessions` re-maps a local terminal id to whatever remote terminal now carries the same name and publishes a spurious `Event::TerminalReattach`.
proposed_fix: Decide the bookkeeping from the request kind rather than from a parity comparison: run `on_detach` whenever the request was a `DetachTerminal` (regardless of the remote's answer — the local client has detached either way) and additionally when an `AttachTerminal` failed. Written out: `if let Some(terminal) = local_terminal && (!attaching || response.is_err()) { sessions::on_detach(...) }`.
test_plan: In `crates/fleet-daemon/tests/router_core.rs`, add `failed_remote_detach_still_releases_the_local_attachment`: wire a `FakeRemote` that answers `AttachTerminal` with `Ack` and `DetachTerminal` with `Err(DaemonError::NotFound(..))`; `forward` an attach then a detach for the same local terminal id; assert via `sessions::attachments_from_shared(&router.terminal_frames.shared_attachments(), &host)` that the host has no remaining attachments. Before the fix the vector still holds `(local, 1)`; after the fix it is empty.
verify_reason: router/mod.rs:168-172 — `attaching != response.is_ok()` is false for a failed DetachTerminal (false != false), so on_detach is skipped. The remote genuinely rejects a stale detach: services/sessions/host_bridge.rs:33-35 starts with host_or_not_found, which returns NotFound once the terminal is removed by close_terminal_if_present (services/sessions/registry.rs:200-244). A transport error on the request has the same effect. on_detach is called from nowhere else in the daemon (only router/mod.rs:162 and :173), so nothing else releases the count. Both downstream consequences check out: the pump is only cancelled when the count reaches zero (router/sessions.rs:113-118) and the Down handler builds tombstones filtered on attachment_count > 0 (router/mod.rs:347-360), which restore_attached_sessions then re-maps and announces as TerminalReattach (router/mod.rs:495-500).
blast_radius: crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/router/mod.rs:168-172 only. The proposed `!attaching || response.is_err()` preserves both existing behaviours (successful detach releases; failed attach releases) and adds only the failed-detach release. Coverage lives in crates/fleet-daemon/tests/router_core.rs; sessions::attachments_from_shared (router/sessions.rs:120) is already pub(crate) for exactly this kind of assertion.

rule: rust-workspace-architecture: hazards-only lint policy — a suppression must be justified; "Does any new lint `allow` carry a `reason`?" (checklist §Manifests)
summary: `Router::with_ids` opens with two no-op statements that exist only to reference two symbols so the dead-code lint stays quiet; one of them keeps a genuinely unused wrapper function alive and both mislead the next reader into thinking the constructor uses them.
failure_scenario: A reader (or a future dead-code sweep) sees two live-looking references at the top of the constructor and concludes both helpers are wired in. Meanwhile `create::ensure_repo_then_create` can drift — its signature can change or its body can rot — with no compiler signal, because the only thing keeping it compiled is a statement whose purpose is to mute the warning.
proposed_fix: Delete both statements. `merge_lifecycle_fanout` is already used, so nothing breaks. Delete the unused `create::ensure_repo_then_create` free wrapper (create.rs:230-241) too, or, if it is meant as a seam for the tests in `crates/fleet-daemon/tests/router_core.rs`, mark it `#[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-support"))]` so its lifetime is stated rather than smuggled.
test_plan: Remove lines 87-88 and run `make clippy`. Before the fix the build is green only because of the suppression; after removing the statements the compiler emits `function ensure_repo_then_create is never used` under `-D warnings`, proving the dead code the statement was hiding. A conformity test asserting `rg -n 'let _ = [a-z_:]+;$' crates/*/src` finds no bare symbol references would fail today at these two lines.
verify_reason: crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/router/mod.rs:85-88 contains both no-op statements verbatim at the top of `with_ids`. `lifecycle::merge_lifecycle_fanout` has three genuine call sites (lifecycle.rs:111, lifecycle.rs:369, translate.rs:321/367), so its line is pure noise. The free `pub(crate) async fn ensure_repo_then_create` at create.rs:230-241 is a one-line delegation to the inherent method (create.rs:48); every other occurrence in the workspace is a method call on the router (dispatch.rs:103, dispatch.rs:244, create.rs:324, create.rs:413, tests/router_core.rs:509-729), and `pub(crate) mod create;` (mod.rs:29) means it is not reachable from outside the crate, so integration tests cannot be the hidden consumer. git log -S dates the statement to ef8639e 'daemon: remote machines contract skeleton and ADR 0011' — leftover scaffolding, not a deliberate seam. Severity is genuinely low; this is hygiene, not a runtime defect.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/router/mod.rs and crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/router/create.rs; nothing else references the free function.
corrected_fix: Delete both statements and delete the free wrapper at create.rs:230-241 (the method is the API; there is no test seam to preserve — router_core.rs uses the method). Skip the proposed `rg 'let _ = [a-z_:]+;$'` conformity test: it would false-positive on legitimate `let _ = tx.send(...)`-shaped lines the moment the pattern is loosened, and clippy under -D warnings already catches the dead code once the crutch is removed. Verify with `cargo clippy -p fleet-daemon --all-targets`.

rule: audit scope: "unbounded growth", "O(n^2) over a collection that grows"
summary: `DiscoveryState::retained` accumulates one entry per finished discovered process and is only ever pruned when the same pid is reused, so it grows without bound and is rescanned in full for every candidate on every discovery pass.
evidence:
crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/watch_discovery.rs:45
```rust
retained: BTreeMap<ProcessIdentity, WatchId>,
```
Inserts, at every process exit (watch_discovery.rs:338, 459, 464):
```rust
if self.watches.finish_discovered(tracked.watch, None).is_ok() {
    self.lock().retained.insert(identity.clone(), tracked.watch);
}
```
The only two removals require the identity to come back as a live candidate: `release_reused_retained` (watch_discovery.rs:342-353) removes only entries `identity.pid == current.pid && *identity != current`, and `retained_watch_is_current` (watch_discovery.rs:361-373) is reached only from the candidate loop (`watch_discovery.rs:185-186`). Nothing drops an entry whose pid is never seen again, and nothing drops it when the underlying watch is expired by `Watches::tick` after its 30-minute `RETENTION` (crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/watches.rs:15, 296-311). `release_reused_retained` is called once per candidate per scan and iterates the whole map:
```rust
let identities = state.retained.keys()
    .filter(|identity| identity.pid == current.pid && *identity != current)
```
failure_scenario: Discovery is enabled with the default interval (>=500 ms, watch_discovery.rs:472-474). An agent terminal spawns short-lived matching subprocesses — on a busy day that is easily tens of thousands. Each exit adds a permanent `(ProcessIdentity, WatchId)` entry; the `WatchId` it names is dropped from `Watches` 30 minutes later, so the entry is pure garbage from then on. After a few days of uptime `retained` holds >10^5 entries and every discovery scan does `candidates × retained` comparisons on the foreground discovery task while holding the `DiscoveryState` mutex, which is the same mutex the 500 ms log-polling pass takes on every tracked process.
proposed_fix: Give `retained` the same liveness discipline the rest of the state has. In `reconcile_tracked`, which already receives `live_identities`, drop retained entries whose watch no longer exists in `Watches` (`watches.watch_for_pid(identity.pid)` returning a different id, or a new `Watches::contains(id)` helper) and whose pid is not live — a single `retain` pass per scan. Since `Watches` already expires entries after `RETENTION`, that pass bounds `retained` by the number of watches actually retained.
test_plan: Add a test in `crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/watch_discovery.rs`'s test module: drive `discover` with a snapshot containing one matching process, then `poll_snapshot` with an empty snapshot so the watch finishes and is retained; `Watches::tick(Instant::now() + RETENTION)` to expire it; then run one more `discover`/`poll_snapshot` cycle with an unrelated snapshot and assert `discovery.lock().retained.is_empty()`. Before the fix the map still holds the dead identity; after the fix it is empty.
verify_reason: watch_discovery.rs:45 declares retained; inserts happen at :335-337 (reconcile_tracked), :455-457 and :461-463 (poll_snapshot). The only removals are release_reused_retained (:341-357) and retained_watch_is_current (:361-373), and both require the pid to come back as a *matching* candidate in the discovery loop (:184-186) — a retained pid later reused by a non-matching process is never pruned, and nothing drops an entry once Watches expires the WatchId after RETENTION (services/watches.rs:15, 296-311). The asymmetry with `environments`, which IS cleaned on finish (:459, :464), makes the omission clear rather than deliberate. Two claims are overstated: growth is bounded by the pid space and each entry is small, and release_reused_retained is candidates × retained where candidates are a handful of agent processes — this is leak-shaped, not an O(n^2) hot spot. Severity is low.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/watch_discovery.rs (reconcile_tracked plus the retained helpers) and its inline mod tests at :827. May need a small `contains`/`watch_for_id` accessor on Watches (crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/watches.rs), whose own tests at watches.rs:~470 would then cover it.
corrected_fix: Prune in reconcile_tracked, but key the pass on the watch, not on pid liveness: an entry whose WatchId no longer exists in Watches is garbage regardless of whether the pid is live, and the existing watch_for_pid check is not sufficient (it returns None for an expired watch and for a pid never re-seen alike). Add a `Watches::contains(WatchId) -> bool` and `state.retained.retain(|_, watch| watches.contains(*watch))` once per scan, outside the per-candidate loop, and take the DiscoveryState lock once for it — do not call it per candidate, or the mutex contention the finding warns about is what the fix introduces.

rule: CLAUDE.md non-negotiable: "Never `let _ =` a fallible call; use `?`, log it, or match it — the one exception is a fire-and-forget channel send, which needs a comment"; rust-workspace-architecture checklist, Errors
summary: `close_terminal_if_present` and `kill_if_present` discard the result of `TerminalHost::kill()` with an uncommented `let _ =`, and because the host-event forwarder thread holds its own `Arc<TerminalHost>`, a failed kill leaks the PTY child, the owner thread and the forwarder thread permanently.
failure_scenario: A terminal is running a program that stops reading stdin (a wedged `ssh`, a paused build) while a client pastes/streams input; the owner's command queue fills to `COMMAND_QUEUE_BYTES` (4 MB). The user closes the tab. `close_terminal_if_present` removes every registry record and calls `host.kill()`, which returns `Err` from `reserve_command_bytes`; the error is dropped on the floor. The session disappears from the snapshot, so nothing can ever address that terminal again — but the PTY child, the owner thread and the `fleet-terminal-events-<n>` thread stay alive for the life of the daemon, holding the worktree directory open. Repeating this leaks one child plus two threads each time, with no log line to explain it.
proposed_fix: Handle the result at both sites: `if let Err(error) = host.kill() { tracing::warn!(%error, terminal = %id, "failed to kill terminal host"); }`, and make the failure recoverable rather than terminal — e.g. have `TerminalHost::kill` bypass the byte budget (a `Kill` command is not user input), or break the retention cycle by having the forwarder thread hold a `Weak<TerminalHost>` so that dropping the registry's `Arc` runs `Drop` and stops the owner.
test_plan: Add `killing_a_terminal_whose_command_queue_is_full_is_reported` in `crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/sessions/tests.rs`: spawn a terminal, fill its command queue past `COMMAND_QUEUE_BYTES` with `paste`, then `close_terminal(terminal).await`, and assert with `tokio::time::timeout` that the child pid reported by the `Terminal` record is no longer alive (`crate::adapters::process::pid_is_alive`). Before the fix the pid stays alive indefinitely and no warning is emitted; after the fix the pid dies (or, at minimum, a captured `tracing` warning names the failure).
verify_reason: services/sessions/registry.rs:238-240 and :281-283 are uncommented `let _ = host.kill()`, which CLAUDE.md forbids outright. kill is fallible for two distinct reasons (fleet-term/src/host.rs:319-321 -> send -> send_command at :332-360): HostError::QueueFull from reserve_command_bytes against COMMAND_QUEUE_BYTES = 4 MiB (host.rs:32, 365-384), and HostError::Closed when the owner receiver is gone. The retention cycle is real: prepare_host_events moves `host: Arc<TerminalHost>` into the forwarder thread which blocks on receiver.recv_blocking (services/sessions/host_bridge.rs:279-291), so dropping the registry's Arc cannot run Drop for TerminalHost (host.rs:423-427) and cannot deliver CommandsClosed, which is what owner.rs:157-160 turns into self.kill(). So on QueueFull the child, the owner thread and the forwarder thread survive with no log line.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/sessions/registry.rs (both sites); if kill is made budget-exempt, crates/fleet-term/src/host.rs (send/send_command/command_bytes) and crates/fleet-term/src/host/owner.rs command draining, plus fleet-term's own host tests. Changing the forwarder to hold a Weak<TerminalHost> touches crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/sessions/host_bridge.rs:276-330 and everything reading host.activity() there, and risks dropping the last Arc mid-frame — the riskier of the two options.
corrected_fix: Do not log every failure at warn as proposed: HostError::Closed is the ordinary case for a terminal whose child already exited and whose owner loop has ended, so an unconditional warn would fire on routine tab closes and on kill_if_present's whole-session sweep. Match instead: `match host.kill() { Ok(()) | Err(HostError::Closed) => {}, Err(error) => tracing::warn!(%error, terminal = %id, "failed to kill terminal host") }`. The substantive half of the fix is making Kill unable to fail on backpressure — give HostCommand::Kill a bypass in send_command (it reserves only COMMAND_OVERHEAD and is not user input) rather than reworking the Arc/Weak ownership, which is the higher-risk change.

rule: CLAUDE.md non-negotiables: "Never `let _ =` a fallible call ... the one exception is a fire-and-forget channel send, which needs a comment saying the receiver is gone only during shutdown."
summary: Several fire-and-forget channel sends in fleet-git and fleet-term use `let _ =` without the comment the project rule requires, so a reader cannot tell a sanctioned drop from an unhandled error.
failure_scenario: Not a runtime failure today: each site is genuinely a send whose receiver is gone only at shutdown. The concrete cost is review and maintenance — `crates/fleet-term/src/host/owner/commands.rs:211-232` drops a `try_send` on a `bounded(1)` reply channel that the attaching client is awaiting, and it is indistinguishable at a glance from the sanctioned shutdown-only drops; a future change that makes that channel legitimately full would silently hang the attach until its deadline instead of erroring. The rule exists precisely so the two cases are separable by grep.
proposed_fix: Add the one-line justification above each sanctioned send, e.g. `// Fire-and-forget: the subscriber is gone only when the last receiver dropped.` in `command_log.rs`, and `// Fire-and-forget: the owner thread has already exited during shutdown.` in `host.rs`/`owner.rs`. For the four attach-reply sites in `commands.rs`, prefer `if reply.try_send(..).is_err() { tracing::warn!(terminal = %self.terminal, "attach requester stopped waiting"); }` since a full or closed reply channel there is a real anomaly, not shutdown.
test_plan: A grep-based conformity test (the same shape the skill recommends for the manifest/layering checks), e.g. `crates/fleet-git/tests/no_bare_discards.rs`: walk `src/**/*.rs`, collect every line matching `let _ = ` outside `#[cfg(test)]`, and assert each has a `//` comment on the preceding non-blank line. It fails today on `command_log.rs:88`, `command_log.rs:93`, `host.rs:426`, `owner.rs:70` and the four `commands.rs` sites, and passes once the comments/handling land.
verify_reason: Verified every cited site: crates/fleet-git/src/command_log.rs:88 and :93 (broadcast sends, no comment), crates/fleet-term/src/host.rs:426 (in `Drop for TerminalHost`, preceded only by a doc comment about the drop semantics, not about the discarded send), crates/fleet-term/src/host/owner.rs:70, and the four `reply.try_send(Err(..))` at crates/fleet-term/src/host/owner/commands.rs:211,215,225,232 — none carry the justification CLAUDE.md requires, while crates/fleet-git/src/watch.rs:67-69 shows the sanctioned form. This is a real but purely conformance-level gap (the finding itself concedes there is no runtime failure). The finding's inventory is also incomplete: bare `let _ =` on fallible non-channel calls also appears at crates/fleet-git/src/command.rs:342,569,570, crates/fleet-git/src/watch.rs:353,392, crates/fleet-git/src/mutation/index.rs:322,334 and crates/fleet-term/src/pty.rs:463 — a fix that only touches the eight cited lines leaves the rule half-applied.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-git/src/command_log.rs, crates/fleet-term/src/host.rs, crates/fleet-term/src/host/owner.rs, crates/fleet-term/src/host/owner/commands.rs; if the attach-reply sites start logging, crates/fleet-term/src/host/owner/tests.rs may need to tolerate the new warnings. No public API changes.
corrected_fix: Add the one-line justification at each sanctioned send, and handle the four attach-reply `try_send`s explicitly (the success path at commands.rs:233 already checks `.is_err()`, so the error paths should match it rather than discard). Drop the proposed `crates/fleet-git/tests/no_bare_discards.rs`: a test that walks `src/**/*.rs` and demands a `//` on the preceding line would fire on every legitimate discard in the crate (`child.kill()`/`child.wait()` at command.rs:569-570, `remove_file` at mutation/index.rs:322,334, `supervisor.await` at command.rs:342) and on test-only sites, is not a shape this workspace uses anywhere (no crate has a source-walking conformity test), and encodes 'comment on the previous line' as if it were the rule. If enforcement is wanted, sweep the remaining sites in the same commit and rely on review plus the existing clippy deny-list in Cargo.toml/clippy.toml.

rule: rust-workspace-architecture: "Write log macros fully qualified — `tracing::warn!`, never `use tracing::warn;` — greppable call sites, no macro collisions." Listed in the skill's anti-pattern table and in the review checklist ("Are log macros fully qualified?").
summary: `fleet-term` imports `tracing::warn` and calls the bare `warn!` macro at 24 sites, against the workspace rule that log macros are always fully qualified.
evidence:
crates/fleet-term/src/ghostty.rs:25
```rust
use tracing::warn;
```
crates/fleet-term/src/host/owner.rs:15
```rust
use tracing::warn;
```
These two imports feed 24 bare call sites (`ghostty.rs` 6, `host/owner.rs` 11, `host/owner/commands.rs` 7), e.g. crates/fleet-term/src/host/owner.rs:200:
```rust
warn!(%error, terminal = %self.terminal, "terminal PTY reader failed");
```
The same crate already writes the qualified form elsewhere — crates/fleet-term/src/pty.rs:373:
```rust
tracing::warn!(%error, "failed to terminate child after PTY setup failure");
```
so the crate is internally inconsistent as well as against the rule. `fleet-core` and `fleet-git` have zero such imports.
failure_scenario: No runtime failure. The concrete cost: `rg 'tracing::warn'` across the workspace misses 24 of fleet-term's warning sites, so a log-level audit or a re-levelling pass (which the skill explicitly calls for — "`warn` is a general-purpose channel there, so re-level as you touch each site") silently skips the terminal host, the noisiest component. It also leaves `warn!` resolvable to any other `warn!` macro a future dependency brings into scope.
proposed_fix: Delete both `use tracing::warn;` lines and qualify the 24 call sites as `tracing::warn!(...)`, matching `crates/fleet-term/src/pty.rs`.
test_plan: Add a conformity test (`crates/fleet-term/tests/logging_conventions.rs`) that walks `src/**/*.rs` and asserts no line matches `^\s*use tracing::(warn|info|error|debug|trace)` and no non-test line contains a bare `warn!(`/`info!(`/`error!(`/`debug!(` not preceded by `tracing::`.
